List the category combinations a filter covers

Source: R/values.R
gcd_values.Rd

Which combinations of category values exist, and how many rows each has, under the same filters as gcd_rows(). It answers "which subjects exist in 2016 at district level?" or "which demographic groups does this county have rows for?" without downloading the rows. The schema's valid_values list every value a column has ever used; gcd_values() lists what exists for this filter, which is what you need when a filter returns zero rows.

The API returns at most 500 combinations; the function warns when that cap is reached.

Usage

gcd_values(
  name,
  columns,
  ...,
  year = NULL,
  detail = NULL,
  district = NULL,
  school = NULL,
  county = NULL
)

Arguments

name

The dataset's name, such as "graduation_rate_4_year_cohort" (see gcd_datasets() and gcd_search()).

columns

One or more categorical columns (or "demographic"), such as "subject" or c("subject", "grade_cluster").

...

Named filters, exactly as in gcd_rows().

year

Years to keep, an integer vector. A run of consecutive years (2019:2024) is sent as a range; anything else (c(2019, 2024)) as exact years. Default NULL: all years.

detail

The one level the rows describe, such as "schools", "districts", "states", "counties" or "tracts". Default NULL: the dataset's default (the finest level, except Census datasets, which default to counties). To combine levels, call once per level and bind the rows.

district, school, county

Places by name, such as district = "Fulton County", school = "Roswell High School", county = c("Fulton", "DeKalb"). Matched exactly against current and former names (ignoring case, accents and a trailing "County"); an unknown or ambiguous name is an error that lists suggestions or candidates. A school name found in more than one district needs district too. For any one place, give its code or its name, not both. Default NULL.

Value

A tibble, most rows first, with one column per requested column (typed from the schema; NA where the column is empty for those rows) and n_rows (integer), the number of rows with that combination.

See also

gcd_rows() for the rows themselves; gcd_describe() for every filter and its allowed values.

Other get data: gcd_rows()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
gcd_values("ccrpi_content_mastery", "subject", year = 2016,
           detail = "districts")
gcd_values("graduation_rate_4_year_cohort", "demographic",
           district = "Fulton County", year = 2024)
}
